title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every even-hole-free graph of degree at most $d$ has tree-width at most $f(d)$.
context_text: Graphs are simple and undirected; a hole is an induced cycle of length at least $4$, it is even or odd according to its number of edges, and a graph is even-hole-free if it has no even hole as an induced subgraph. Here 'degree at most $d$' means maximum degree at most $d$. The class of all even-hole-free graphs has unbounded tree-width (it contains all complete graphs and all chordal graphs), even-hole-free graphs with no triangle have bounded tree-width, but Sintiari and Trotignon constructed (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs of unbounded tree-width; that construction uses vertices of large degree and large clique minors, which motivates the conjecture. If true, it would imply that even-hole-freeness is testable with constant query complexity and polylogarithmic running time in the bounded-degree graph model of property testing, via CMSO testability on graphs of bounded degree and bounded tree-width. The authors prove that every even-hole-free graph excluding $K_\ell$ as a minor has tree-width bounded by a function of $\ell$, prove the conjecture for $d\le 3$ (every subcubic even-hole-free graph, and even every subcubic (theta, prism)-free graph, has tree-width at most $3$), and prove for $d=4$ the weaker statement that (even hole, pyramid)-free graphs of maximum degree at most $4$ have bounded tree-width. The conjecture is trivial for $d\le 2$.
paper_title: On the tree-width of even-hole-free graphs

title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f_d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every graph with degree at most $d$ and tree-width at least $f_d(k)$ contains a $(k \times k)$-wall or the line graph of a $(k \times k)$-wall as an induced subgraph.
context_text: Graphs are simple and undirected; 'degree at most $d$' means maximum degree at most $d$. An elementary $(k\times k)$-wall is the usual wall of the excluded-grid theorem: a hexagonal grid (brick wall) of maximum degree $3$ with $k$ horizontal paths and $k$ vertical paths; a $(k\times k)$-wall is any subdivision of an elementary $(k\times k)$-wall. Robertson and Seymour proved that graphs of large tree-width contain a large wall as a subgraph; this cannot be strengthened to induced subgraphs in general, since $K_n$ has tree-width $n-1$. The authors prove an induced grid theorem for minor-free graphs: for every graph $H$ there is $f_H$ such that every $H$-minor-free graph of tree-width at least $f_H(k)$ contains a $(k\times k)$-wall or the line graph of a chordless $(k\times k)$-wall (a graph is chordless if no cycle of length at least $4$ has a chord) as an induced subgraph. Graphs with no induced subdivision of a $6\times 3$ wall and with arbitrarily large tree-width and girth exist, but their construction (like that of (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs of unbounded tree-width) needs vertices of large degree and large clique minors, which motivates this bounded-degree analogue. It is described as wide open, and it implies the authors' conjecture that even-hole-free graphs of bounded degree have bounded tree-width. Status note (November 2026): proved by Korhonen ('Grid induced minor theorem for graphs of small degree', arXiv 2203.13233, 2022; J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2023): graphs of maximum degree at most $d$ and treewidth at least $f(k,d)=O(k^{10}+2^{d^5})$ contain the $k\times k$ grid as an induced minor, which together with the routing arguments of Aboulker, Adler, Kim, Sintiari and Trotignon gives the wall statement.
paper_title: On the tree-width of even-hole-free graphs
